note: Registry of pre-auth surfaces for the enumeration-boundary parity harness (test/example/test/example_web/enumeration_parity_test.exs). A row with state parity proves ONLY the listed compare dimensions, for ONE request issued for an existing identity and for an unknown identity, and nothing else (not timing, not repeat attempts, not locked or unconfirmed accounts). The harness runs in the example host, a hand-maintained copy of the generated host that already drifts from the generated templates; only install_smoke proves a generated host. States: parity (must compare same), known_divergence (must still differ; fixing the product forces this row to be removed or changed), by_design (documented behaviour is asserted), not_proven (no assertion; blocker cites the file:line that prevents a deterministic probe).

surfaces.note: Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. One failed attempt (wrong password) for an existing email versus any password for an unknown email, fresh state: no earlier failures, account not locked. Compares the POST status, redirect location, server-side flash map and the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email. Repeat attempts (lockout), timing and the locked and unconfirmed states are NOT compared; see password-signin-repeat-attempts.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. One magic-link request for an existing email versus an unknown email, fresh state. Compares the POST status, redirect location, server-side flash map and the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email. Email delivery (presence and subject), timing and the library rate limit are NOT compared; see magic-link-rate-limit.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. Not proven: the example host cannot drive the request form, so no response is compared. The route has no :new live action and the view raises on mount (verified by running it). The same view passes a user struct to Example.Accounts.deliver_user_reset_password_instructions/2, whose head requires a binary email (read in source, not executed). Generated hosts are not covered by this row.
surfaces.blocker: test/example/lib/example_web/router.ex:112 routes /users/reset-password without the :new live action, so ExampleWeb.ResetPasswordLive.mount/3 raises CaseClauseError at test/example/lib/example_web/live/reset_password_live.ex:146 before any request can be compared

surfaces.note: Identity = the session user (the resend event takes no email). Not proven: the example host cannot drive resend for either session state, so no response is compared. Anonymous visitors mount with current_scope nil and the handler raises BadMapError; signed-in visitors are redirected to /app before mount (both verified by running it). The generated confirm routes have the same defect, tracked by the linked todo.
surfaces.blocker: test/example/lib/example_web/live/confirmation_live.ex:158 reads socket.assigns.current_scope.user in the resend handler, and test/example/lib/example_web/router.ex:106 redirects signed-in visitors before mount, so neither session state can complete a resend

surfaces.note: Identity = code kind, not account existence: for a user with an MFA-pending session, one wrong authenticator code (existing) versus one wrong backup code (unknown), each on a freshly enrolled user. Compares the outcome (re-rendered in place, reported as 200), redirect location and the flash message including the remaining-attempts count. The flash is read from the LiveView process state because the view does not render it in its own markup. The body is NOT compared: the authenticator and backup panels differ by design. A pending versus absent MFA session and the lockout outcome are NOT compared.
